evidenceBoundary.reason: No authorization was given to write fixtures into external Google, Microsoft, or Apple accounts.

findings.claim: VCALENDAR is a container for sibling calendar components; VEVENT, VTODO, and VJOURNAL are not physically nested inside one another.

For the ordinary publish/import object used by this lab, a scheduled VEVENT requires DTSTART. The RFC has special scheduling-object qualifications, so the lab does not generalize this to every possible METHOD-bearing object.
VTODO can omit DTSTART and DUE, but that does not prove that consumer calendar clients will expose or preserve it as a FlowMe backlog task.
RELATED-TO references another component UID, but target systems own the behavioral implications of the relationship.
X-properties may be ignored by user agents, so X-FLOWME fields cannot be the only canonical store for hierarchy, provenance, rights, or review meaning.
Google officially documents ICS/CSV event import and event export, but the reviewed user and API documentation does not promise VTODO, VJOURNAL, RELATED-TO, or X-property preservation.

Microsoft documents importing calendar events from ICS and provides separate event and To Do task APIs; preservation of VTODO, VJOURNAL, RELATED-TO, and X-properties is not proven by the reviewed UI documentation.
Apple documents Calendar event import/export and separately describes Reminders integration; this does not prove that imported ICS VTODO becomes or round-trips as a Reminder.

forbiddenClaimsWithoutExternalTest: VTODO appears as a task or reminder in a target client
RELATED-TO hierarchy survives import and export
X-FLOWME properties survive import and export
recurrence exceptions and completion states survive cross-client round-trip
